target_customer: County and local government tax assessors, clerks and front desk staff in the United States
problem: Local governments process reams of paper when property changes ownership before updating tax rolls. The company builds software to make that deeds and change of ownership workflow faster.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to local governments

founders.name: Imran Khoja
previous_startups: Two social enterprises (names and outcomes not stated)
founders.background_notes: From the company's about page. The company says it started out of Stanford Business School.

founders.name: Travis Noll
prior_employers: Healthcare and pharmaceutical strategy consulting (employer not named)
education: Stanford, BS and MS Management Science and Engineering, and MBA
founders.background_notes: Company page does not say he is a co-founder, but the YC page lists him as Founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Document processing and integration with legacy county systems was standard engineering with hard integration work; AI features became feasible later.

defensibility.rationale: Once embedded in county workflows and integrated into legacy systems, government customers rarely switch, though entrenched vendors could bundle similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: An analysis page says entrenched vendors can bundle similar workflows; no source shows an incumbent acquiring or copying the product.

market_need_then: Local governments relied on paper deeds and manual processing at the change of ownership step, per the company description.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission language about empowering local government employees

rebrands.why: Not stated; the about page links to a letter about the new name and the footer still reads Just Appraised Inc.

brand_strength.rationale: Niche B2B brand; descriptive original name tied to appraisals while products expanded to clerks and front desks, which prompted a rename.

outcome_analysis: Just Appraised grew from deeds automation for assessors in 2017 to products for clerks and front desks, and says it serves 300 plus counties in 30 plus states. It raised a Series A in 2024 per aggregators, and rebranded to Alltus. Sticky government workflows helped while sales cycles stayed slow.
notes: Series A of 12.3M USD in April 2024 appears in PitchBook and VCBacked summaries; Caplight lists a different date and a total of 24.82M USD and a headline for a different company, so amounts conflict and investors beyond Highland are not recorded. A 2017 seed of about 120K USD is on one aggregator only (StartupIntros) and a 2022 round on yespress only, both unverified. Rename date unknown. Competitor search found only undated aggregator and analysis pages (Tyler Technologies, gTerra, TaxProper), so the dated list is empty. Funding figures come from search result summaries, not opened pages.
